Day 3 was a redone of some work and practice. 
remembering important points 

Openai popularity forced other provider to offer their services on openai endpoint 

each LLM call has two main components Clients and Response 
Clients itself has two components, base url and api key 
responses has two components model and messages, additionally, messages has two components as well, role and content 

client = OpenAI(model, base_url)
response = client.chat.completions.create(model, messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "some text here!"}]) 
Always remember the above

assert 2+2 == 4

Import important packages 

```{python}
import tiktoken

encoding = tiktoken.encoding_for_model(model_name="gpt-4.1-mini")
tokens = encoding.encode("Hi, my name is Mosa and I like salad soup!")
tokens

```

reversing the tokens 

```{python}

for token_id in tokens: 
  token_text = encoding.decode([token_id])
  print(f"The token id {token_id} == {token_text}")

```

Task: 
bring your packages and api keys to your current session 

```{python}
import os 
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from openai import OpenAI
load_dotenv(override=True)

deepseek_api_key = os.getenv("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY")
### verify the deepseek key 
if not deepseek_api_key: 
  print("there is no deepseek api key ")
elif not deepseek_api_key.startswith("sk-"):
  print("The key doesn't start with sk0")
else: 
  print("Your DeepSeek Api Key is ready to use. ")

### here deepseek is the client. It needs two things: base url and base model 
deepseek = OpenAI(api_key=deepseek_api_key, base_url="https://api.deepseek.com")
### changing the fun facts to make sure the model is working 
response = deepseek.chat.completions.create(model="deepseek-chat", messages = [
  {"role": "user", "content": "Tell me a fun fact about Tajikistan."}
])

print(f"the model is {response.model} \nthe fun fact: {response.choices[0].message.content}")



```

create the same thing for openai 

```{python}
### do everything from scratch 
import os 
from openai import OpenAI
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv(override=True)

openai_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")

### Later I can create a module to verify if the key 
if not openai_key: 
  print("The openai key doesn't exisit.") 
elif not openai_key.startswith("sk-proj-"):
  print("The right openai key doesn't exist")
else: 
  print("Your Openai Api Key is ready to use. Enjoy LLM engineering!")

### Create the client 
openai_client = OpenAI(api_key=openai_key, base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1")

# create the response 
response = openai_client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-6-luna", messages=[
  {"role": "user", "content": "Tell me a fun fact about Afghanistan!"}
])

response.choices[0].message.content

```

recreating the lecture 
### Two types of Messages 
#### System message 
#### User message


```{python}
from openai import OpenAI

openai = OpenAI()

### below creating messages, 
## there are two messages, one is system message and the other is user message 
messages = [
  {"role": "system", "content": "You are a professional helpful assistant."}, 
  {"role": "user", "content": "Hi!, my name is Mosa Rahimi. "}
]

response = openai.chat.completions.create(model = "gpt-6-luna", messages = messages)
response.choices[0].message.content

```
below if I change the message and change the user message, even though above I gave my name to it, the luna will not know my name. 

```{python}
messages = [
  {"role": "system", "content": "You are a professional helpful assistant."}, 
  {"role": "user", "content": "What is my name? Do you know it? "}
]
response = openai.chat.completions.create(model = "gpt-6-luna", messages=messages)
response.choices[0].message.content 

```

The two chunk code above shows that the LLM are stateless, meaning they don't have memory 

Below example adds memory to the chat, in fact it creates context 

```{python}
messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Hi! I'm Mosa Rahimi!"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi Mosa Rahimi! How can I assist you today?"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "What's my name?"}
    ]

response = openai.chat.completions.create(model = "gpt-6-luna", messages=messages)
response.choices[0].message.content

```
